summary: A Continental Divide lookout on the Helena National Forest, rebuilt in 1962 (per two of three sources), one of only four lookouts left on that forest, now a rental.

facts.design: 15x15 ft R-6 flat cab on a treated wood tower (original 1932 structure was an L-4 cab on a 20-foot tower)

access.note: Open to the public as a Recreation.gov rental; access road rough toward the end, high-clearance vehicle recommended

visit.trail_note: Directly on the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail, which passes by the tower

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest, Lincoln Ranger District

events.note: NHLR and Recreation.gov both date the first lookout, an L-4 cab on a 20-foot tower, to 1932
firelookout.com instead dates the original L-4 tower's construction to 1934, disagreeing with the other two sources
firelookout.com says the present 20-foot treated-timber tower with R-6 flat cab was built in 1954
NHLR and Recreation.gov instead date the current 15x15 ft R-6 flat cab on a treated wood tower to 1962
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register October 15, 2008
Added to the Recreation Rental program in 2016, per firelookout.com

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Recreation.gov agree on 1932 (original) and 1962 (replacement). firelookout.com instead gives 1934 and 1954. The story follows the two agreeing sources for its main narrative but notes the firelookout.com discrepancy explicitly rather than omitting it.

sources.title: Granite Butte Lookout, Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest

evidence.supports: one of only four remaining on Helena NF, first lookout L-4 cab on 20ft tower built 1932, present 15x15 R-6 flat cab on treated wood tower built 1962, elevation 6887 ft
evidence.quote: Granite Butte Lookout is one of only four remaining on the Helena National Forest. The first lookout on this site was an L-4 cab on a 20' tower built in 1932. This 15'x15' R-6 flat cab on a treated wood tower was constructed in 1962.

evidence.supports: elevation 7587 ft, 15x15 cabin on 20ft tower first built 1932, rebuilt 1962, recently renovated, NHLR listing 2008, Continental Divide Trail access, road rough high-clearance, facilities, no electricity/plumbing, vault toilet, winter recreation
evidence.quote: The 15' by 15' lookout cabin sits atop a 20' tall wooden tower that was first built in 1932. The structure was rebuilt in 1962 and has been recently renovated. This tower was listed on the national register of historic lookouts in 2008

evidence.supports: developed 1934 with 20ft L-4 tower, present 20ft treated timber R-6 flat cab tower built 1954, staffed into 1990s, added to Recreation Rental program 2016
evidence.quote: Developed in 1934 with a 20' L-4 tower, the present 20' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab was built in 1954. It was staffed into the 1990's, and was added to the Recreation Rental program in 2016.

notes_for_editor: Elevation differs notably between NHLR (6,887 ft / 2,099 m, matching the brief's elevation_m field) and Recreation.gov (7,587 ft) -- flagged in the story rather than silently picking one, since neither page explains the gap and it's larger than a rounding difference. Build-year conflict between firelookout.com (1934/1954) and NHLR+Recreation.gov (1932/1962) also flagged; went with the two-source majority for the main narrative. No staffing-end date is corroborated outside firelookout.com, so that claim is attributed to it alone. No NRHP nomination PDF or newspaper source found in two web searches; confidence is medium given the unresolved elevation and date conflicts.
